column3: NKJV has “a great sound of a trumpet,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “a great trumpet.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV has “it is near,” where the Greek may also be read “He is near.”
NKJV omits “nor the Son,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it. “The Father” is rendered “My Father,” also from the Textus Receptus.
NKJV has “what hour,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “on what day.”
NKJV has “delaying his coming,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “My master delays.”
Close to the Greek; “will appoint his place” is rendered “appoint him his portion.”
